AttributeList.Text: Scrubber inputs, saved trips, drain timers and valve output commands.
LSH-102 input OFF means high level or loss of the healthy signal; this alarm follows the input. Reference: C04 / H-10.
Show the high-level input alarm
PSH-101 input OFF activates the current pressure alarm; trip memory is separate. Reference: C03 / H-10.
Show the high-pressure input alarm
LSHH-103 input OFF activates the current high-high-level alarm. Reference: C05 / H-10.
Show the very-high-level input alarm
RESET is accepted with pressure and very-high-level inputs healthy and common E-STOP permission restored. Reference: C03 / C05 / C01.
Reset scrubber trips after recovery
Latch on pressure trip, very-high-level trip, E-STOP or first scan; cancel both burner START permissions through their blocks. Reference: S-01 / C01 / C03 / C05.
Trip the suction and block both burners
Latch on pressure trip, E-STOP or first scan. Very-high level alone does not open the flare. Reference: S-01 / C01 / C03.
Trip the flare on pressure or E-STOP
XV-401 is normally open: output ON energizes the coil to close it. No position feedback is available. Reference: E5.
Send the flare CLOSE command
XV-403 is normally closed: output ON requests opening while no suction trip is latched. Reference: E7.
Send the suction OPEN command
Both trip latches are clear. This is not proof of valve position and does not describe the drain. Reference: S-01.
Show normal flare and suction commands
Either level input OFF requests level handling, including a possible lost healthy signal. Reference: C04 / C05 / H-10.
Detect a high-level demand
Continuous high-level demand for the accepted opening delay sets the drain demand. Reference: C04.
Delay the drain OPEN request
With both level inputs healthy throughout the closing delay, clear the drain demand. Reference: C04.
Delay the drain CLOSE request
Time the actual drain output command; on expiry remember the timeout and remove its OPEN command. Reference: C04a.
Limit continuous drain opening
RESET clears this timeout even if high-level demand remains; the OPEN command may return immediately. Reference: C04a.
Reset the drain timeout
Need saved drain demand, E-STOP permission and no drain timeout. A scrubber trip alone does not block the drain. Reference: E6.
Send the drain OPEN command
If LSHH-103 signals very-high level while LSH-102 stays healthy for 5 seconds, remember a level-switch fault. Reference: C04b / H-10.
Detect inconsistent level inputs
RESET needs the impossible combination to be gone: NOT LSH or LSHH. The two inputs need not be equal. Reference: C04b / H-10.
Reset the level-input mismatch fault
Remember this cause until a healthy RESET; a saved cause is not proof that the input is still abnormal. Reference: C06a.
Remember the E-STOP trip cause
Remember this cause until a healthy RESET; a saved cause is not proof that the input is still abnormal. Reference: C06a / H-10.
Remember the high pressure trip cause
Remember this cause until a healthy RESET; a saved cause is not proof that the input is still abnormal. Reference: C06a / H-10.
Remember the very-high level trip cause
Remember this cause until a healthy RESET; a saved cause is not proof that the input is still abnormal. Reference: C06a.
Remember the power-up trip cause
Write only while no first cause is saved. Simultaneous causes use network order: E-STOP, pressure, very-high level, power-up. Reference: C06a.
Record E-STOP as the first trip cause
Write only while no first cause is saved. Simultaneous causes use network order: E-STOP, pressure, very-high level, power-up. Reference: C06a / H-10.
Record high pressure as the first trip cause
Write only while no first cause is saved. Simultaneous causes use network order: E-STOP, pressure, very-high level, power-up. Reference: C06a / H-10.
Record very-high level as the first trip cause
Write only while no first cause is saved. Simultaneous causes use network order: E-STOP, pressure, very-high level, power-up. Reference: C06a.
Record power-up as the first trip cause
Healthy RESET clears all saved causes and the first-cause code; this network runs after recording. Reference: C06a.
Clear trip-cause memory after recovery
Scrubber
